plugins.name: agent-adversarial-challenger

The critic half of a generate/critique loop; debugging escalation, debate devil's-advocate, research and decision review are all applications.

Ships `coder` (edits the caller's tree directly; the parent commits) and `parallel-coder` (runs in an isolated worktree, self-commits, and hands back a reviewable branch — for parallel or staged work). Claude also gets a top-level edit reminder; Codex relies on steering because tool-hook payloads do not identify subagent edits.

plugins.name: beads

Ships steering that scopes beads against SpecKit artifacts (requirements) and TaskCreate (single-session scratch) and fixes conventions for labels vs structured fields vs metadata, actor identity, claim etiquette, JSON envelope determinism, and Dolt sync. Session-start wiring is native: run `bd setup claude --global` once (SessionStart bd prime injection) and `bd init --skip-hooks` per repo. Contributor skills (architecture, backend, release, testing) are omitted. Third-party (manaflow-ai/cmux publishes no APM/marketplace manifest); referenced as raw GitHub skill paths, same pattern as the other external bundles.

plugins.name: dep-update

plugins.name: frontend

plugins.name: governance

plugins.name: handover

plugins.name: headroom
plugins.description: Run coding agents through Headroom to compress context and cut token usage (~60-95% fewer) and to read token-savings stats.

plugins.name: hooks-attribution-guard
plugins.description: Advises against AI authorship attribution in git commits (Co-Authored-By Claude/Anthropic, "Generated with/by AI", "AI-assisted/AI-generated", Claude Code trailers). Emits a non-blocking advisory (allow + additionalContext, exit 0) so the human stays the sole author of record. Scoped to attribution trailers/phrases so prose mentioning AI is not flagged. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-bash-safety
plugins.description: Bash safety guards tuned for autonomous agents: hard-block only unrecoverable ops (rm -rf / or $HOME root, mkfs, dd to a real block device, sandbox-bypass flag). dd to pseudo-devices (/dev/null, /dev/zero, /dev/random, /dev/urandom, /dev/stdout, /dev/stdin) is allowed. curl|sh pipes emit a non-blocking warn (allow + advisory). sudo paired with destructive/disruptive verbs also warns. rm -rf defers to rm-rf-guard: project-local and temp-dir cleanups are silent; unexpanded $var targets are denied; ~/subpath, repo root/.git, and outside-tree paths warn (non-blocking). Quoted bypass forms (rm -rf "/etc") and flags-after-target (rm /path -rf) are denied. Matching is anchored to command position to avoid quoted-string false positives. No "ask" is ever emitted. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-chezmoi-guard
plugins.description: PreToolUse advisory (non-blocking) for files chezmoi ACTUALLY manages (exact membership in `chezmoi managed`, 60s cache). Emits permissionDecision:"allow" + additionalContext steering changes to the chezmoi source — the operation proceeds. Read-only references and unmanaged paths are silent. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-close-keywords
plugins.description: Fixes the GitHub "comma-list close" quirk, where a closing keyword binds to only the FIRST issue in a list (Closes #1, #2, #3 closes just #1). A shared normalizer distributes the keyword across every issue in a contiguous list (-> Closes #1, closes #2, closes #3) for close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved. Two delivery layers: a pre-commit commit-msg hook that rewrites the message in place (tool-agnostic), and a PreToolUse guard on `gh pr create`/`gh pr edit` that emits a non-blocking advisory (allow + additionalContext carrying the corrected body) when a malformed comma-list close is detected. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-git-safety
plugins.description: Git safety guards tuned for autonomous agents. DENY only when a destructive op targets another working tree through an unexpanded shell variable or ~ (the guard cannot verify the target — agent re-issues with a literal path). All other destructive ops are non-blocking: reset --hard / checkout -- / restore / clean -f emit a warn (allow + advisory) only when uncommitted work would actually be lost; push --force/--force-with-lease always warns. branch -D, tag -d, stash drop/clear, worktree remove --force are passed silently (all reflog-recoverable). No "ask" is ever emitted. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-git-workflow
plugins.description: Opt-in git workflow hook: warn about uncommitted AND unpushed work at session end (continuous commit/push cadence). Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-package-investigate
plugins.description: Non-blocking PreToolUse Bash hook that nudges the agent to investigate a dependency's trustworthiness, maintenance, quality, popularity, and alternatives BEFORE adding/installing it (lighter review for update/upgrade/remove). Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-portability-ci
plugins.description: CI gate that runs shipped hook scripts through the real portability failure modes the audits found: bash 3.2 parse errors (;;& fallthrough, mapfile), GNU-only sed/grep constructs (\b word boundaries, lazy quantifiers), and string-form tool_input payloads that crash jq. Reports a summary and exits non-zero on any failure. Invoked on demand or wired into CI.

plugins.name: hooks-precommit-gate
plugins.description: PreToolUse advisory (non-blocking) for git commit/push when a repo opts into the pre-commit framework. When the repo has .pre-commit-config.yaml but the matching git hook is not installed, or --no-verify would skip the framework, emits a single permissionDecision:"allow" + additionalContext advisory — the operation proceeds. Silent in repos with no pre-commit config, so it adds zero friction elsewhere. Pairs with secrets-scan (enforcement lives in the pre-push hook). Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-quality
plugins.description: Opt-in code-quality hooks: advisory linting/formatting feedback after edits and a quality check before commits. The before-commit gate is a FALLBACK — it defers when the pre-commit framework is installed (which already runs the same formatters), so it only fires in repos that have not adopted pre-commit. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: hooks-subagent-model
plugins.description: Model-routing deny gate for subagent spawns. A PreToolUse:Agent hook DENIES an Agent/Task call when `model` is omitted AND the named subagent_type has no pinned model in its definition (or subagent_type itself is omitted) — the spawn would otherwise silently inherit the parent session's model, often an expensive top-tier one. The deny reason is a tier routing table (cheap tier for mechanical work, mid tier for bounded coding/research, top tier or an explicit session-model pass-through for deep/adversarial work) so the caller's retry succeeds. The deny reason also notes that reasoning effort is NOT enforceable per-call (no `effort` field exists on the Agent tool_input) and points to pinning `effort:` in reusable agent definitions instead. The inherit-by-default type list is overridable per-project via SUBAGENT_MODEL_GUARD_INHERIT_TYPES. Fails open on malformed input. Claude-only (the Agent spawn tool is Claude-specific); the Codex variant is a no-op.

plugins.name: hooks-subagent-worktree
plugins.description: Non-blocking worktree-isolation advisory on every subagent spawn. A PreToolUse:Agent hook injects a short reminder — if the subagent WRITES files and runs in parallel with other writers, pass `isolation:"worktree"` (Claude branches it from your current HEAD); a read-only, different-repo, or lone-writer subagent needs none — and if it does run isolated, to COMMIT before finishing so the worktree branch retains the work. It NEVER denies a spawn (superseding the 1.x deny-gate, which guessed wrong and blocked legitimate work) and stays silent once isolation is already declared. Claude-only (the Agent spawn tool is Claude-specific); the Codex variant is a no-op.

plugins.name: hooks-worktree
plugins.description: Worktree lifecycle hooks: create worktrees outside the repo tree (in /tmp) to prevent nesting, and clean up the worktree directory and branch on removal. Claude-only WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove events; Codex requires explicit worktree wrapper commands because it has no equivalent lifecycle events.

plugins.name: matt-skills
plugins.description: Bundle of Matt Pocock's engineering and productivity skills: grilling, grill-with-docs, tdd, to-prd, to-issues, triage, improve-codebase-architecture, and setup.

plugins.name: mcp-codebase-memory
plugins.description: MCP server package for the Codebase Memory MCP, providing graph-aware project orientation (symbol search, call paths, code snippets).

plugins.name: mcp-context7
plugins.description: MCP server package for Context7, providing current library and framework documentation lookups.

plugins.name: mcp-mempalace
plugins.description: MCP server package for MemPalace, a local-first cross-session memory layer for coding agents. Files verbatim conversation/decision history into a vector + temporal-graph store (ChromaDB, local embeddings, zero LLM calls) and recalls it via semantic + temporal search. Ships the mempalace-mcp stdio server, a SessionStart hook that injects a tiny per-repo memory index (recall happens on demand via mempalace_search with a real query), a SessionEnd hook that automatically mines each completed session's transcript into the repo's wing (with FTS5 self-heal), a one-time backfill script for historical transcripts, and steering that scopes MemPalace (cross-session memory) against codebase-memory (current code structure). Complements code intelligence; it is not code navigation.

plugins.name: mcp-package-version
plugins.description: MCP server for package version discovery

plugins.name: mcp-playwright
plugins.description: MCP server package for Playwright, providing browser automation and in-browser UI verification.

plugins.name: mcp-repomix
plugins.description: MCP server package for Repomix, providing bulk repository snapshots for analysis and review.

plugins.name: mcp-serena
plugins.description: MCP server package for Serena semantic code tools. The launcher selects the Codex or Claude Code context from the parent harness and can be overridden with SERENA_MCP_CONTEXT.

plugins.name: mcp-tauri
plugins.description: MCP server package for Tauri, enabling AI assistants to build, test, and debug Tauri v2 apps — UI automation, IPC monitoring, log streaming, mobile device listing, and plugin setup.

plugins.name: orchestrate
plugins.description: Orchestrate a fleet of subagents across complex, parallel, or long-running work while controlling cost by routing each role to the cheapest capable model. Run state (task DAG, claims, audit trail, merge coordination) lives in beads (the bd CLI, a hard prerequisite). Ships the orchestration playbook plus bundled agents (workflow-coder, workflow-reviewer, workflow-advisor, integration-gatekeeper, ledger-scribe), a Claude skill-scoped SubagentStart comms hook, explicit Codex spawn-brief protocol, and deterministic scripts (scope disjointness, agent discovery, conflict probe).

plugins.name: planning-product
plugins.description: Planning and product toolkit: the debate, eli5, and web-fetch skills plus Matt's PRD, issue-writing, TDD, triage, and architecture-improvement workflows.

plugins.name: playwright
plugins.description: Automate browser tasks through a Playwright MCP server: navigate, click, fill forms, and extract page data.

plugins.name: pr-shepherd
plugins.description: Cross-session PR/merge shepherd with beads (bd) as the central state store. Merge work lives as beads labeled agent:integrator with gh:pr/gh:run gate beads owning async waits; any session (or a /loop or cron invocation) drains the queue: bd gate check, atomic claim, merge-tree conflict probe + gh PR state, then either a slot-guarded merge or a bounce-back fix bead routed to agent:coder that parks the merge bead until fixed. Ships the pr-shepherd skill, a standalone pr-shepherd agent, steering for the merge-bead lifecycle and bounce-back protocol, and an advisory Stop hook that reminds when the integrator queue is non-empty. Requires the bd CLI (gastownhall/beads >= 1.1.0) and gh; all parts are inert in repos without .beads/.

plugins.name: presentation
plugins.description: Presentation bundle for general decks, Marp slides, and PowerPoint template workflows.

plugins.name: project-lifecycle
plugins.description: Day-to-day project lifecycle workflows: resume work after interruption (catchup), write handovers, and run verification. Bundles the matching skills, git-workflow steering, and the PR reviewer agent.

plugins.name: python-quality
plugins.description: Run Python format, lint, type-check, and test commands with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: release-please
plugins.description: Drive releases with googleapis/release-please. Use for any release, tagging, changelog, or version-bump work, and whenever the repo has a release-please-config.json / .release-please-manifest.json or a release-please workflow -- then following release-please is mandatory. Also use to set up release-please in a repo. Covers setup, the git/commit process, publishing, monorepo/manifest config, and diagnosing and recovering stuck or botched releases. Ships a warn-only cross-tool advisory hook; it never blocks.

plugins.name: resume-cv
plugins.description: CV / career-resume bundle: focused resume-tailoring and broad career-support workflows. Renamed from `resume` to avoid a namespace collision with `resume-session` (which resumes a prior coding SESSION, not a CV).

plugins.name: resume-session
plugins.description: Resume a previous agent session in the current repository from its transcript, reading only the latest context incrementally instead of reloading the full history. Discovers prior Claude Code and Codex sessions, summarizes the leftoff state, confirms ambiguities, then continues the work.

plugins.name: review
plugins.description: Code review and verification toolkit: the verify skill and the PR reviewer agent, and Hobson comprehensive-review, performance-testing-review, unit-testing, and tdd-workflows plugins. Language-specific quality checks live in the language-<lang> bundles.

plugins.name: rust-quality
plugins.description: Run Rust format, lint, and test checks with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: secrets-scan
plugins.description: Pre-commit secret scanning. A skill plus a PreToolUse hook that runs gitleaks or trufflehog (whichever is on PATH) over staged changes and blocks the commit when a secret is found, with an actionable message and a documented bypass. Warns and allows when no scanner is installed, so missing tooling never blocks. Cross-tool (Claude + Codex).

plugins.name: security
plugins.description: Security toolkit: Hobson security-scanning, security-compliance, backend-api-security, frontend-mobile-security, and reverse-engineering plugins for vulnerability analysis, compliance, and hardening.

plugins.name: session-review
plugins.description: Audit the ending session for corrections, lessons, unresolved TODOs, and follow-up work, then recommend handoffs to `handover`, `audit-steering`, or `write-agentic`. Use when the user says wrap up, review this session, what did we learn, or before a handover.

plugins.name: sniff
plugins.description: Refactoring auditor. Detects code smells, tech debt, and non-idiomatic code across 21 languages and formats, maps each finding to refactoring.guru smells, patterns, and techniques, stress-tests every recommendation with a built-in adversarial pragmatism critic, and produces a prioritized refactoring plan (impact, value, cost, severity, backwards-compatibility). Drives each language toolchain's own linters and analyzers (opportunistic, never required) with a guided first-run installer. Advisory by default; applies low-risk refactors only on explicit approval behind a verification re-run. Standalone: no APM dependencies.

plugins.name: speckit
plugins.description: SpecKit mechanism: the six SpecKit agents and the bugfix and setup skills. Opt into the opinionated layers separately: steering-speckit (the mandatory-gated workflow); workflow gates are beads gate beads provisioned by the speckit-beads formula during setup.

plugins.name: speckit-beads
plugins.description: Beads-native SpecKit workflow: ships the speckit-feature bd formula (the SpecKit phase spine as a molecule DAG with human gates at clarify approval, analyze approval, and verify sign-off), steering that maps one spec dir to one molecule root epic and implementation task beads to the implement step, and a PreToolUse guard that denies every Write/Edit to specs/*/tasks.md when a beads workspace is active — task state lives in beads and tasks.md is never authored (reads stay allowed for legacy migration). Replaces the archived speckit-gate gates.yaml engine. Requires the bd CLI (gastownhall/beads >= 1.1.0); guard and steering are inert in repos without .beads/. Install the formula by copying formulas/speckit-feature.formula.toml into the repo's .beads/formulas/.

plugins.name: steering-architecture
plugins.description: Cross-cutting design steering: compose over fork, keep generic cores case-agnostic, and make structural invariants a verifiable diff guard. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-backend
plugins.description: Opinionated backend conventions: service/function/worker runtime shape, API and cross-boundary contract rules, and background-job (queue, event, scheduled) patterns. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-data
plugins.description: Opinionated data conventions: data ownership, database assets, migrations, pipelines, and notebook practices. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-delivery
plugins.description: Opinionated delivery cadence: work like a developer who commits continuously. Commit and push after every meaningful, self-contained step; keep commits atomic; leave no unpushed local work stranded in a local or disposable worktree. Always-on steering. Opt-in.

plugins.name: steering-docs-specs
plugins.description: Spec and SpecKit workflow conventions: spec modes, specs/ placement, and .specify/ asset separation. Doc-writing style rules live in the write-docs package. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-frontend
plugins.description: Opinionated frontend conventions: framework choice by surface (React/Vue/Next/Astro), UI library picks, app vs server state, and browser verification expectations. Opt-in steering -- install to adopt these frontend defaults.

plugins.name: steering-git-workflow
plugins.description: Git workflow policy: branch discipline, ship-path choice (merge vs PR), merge flags, and pre-push verification. Replaces the retired commit-push-* skills and git nudge hooks.

plugins.name: steering-infrastructure
plugins.description: Opinionated infrastructure conventions: platform code, IaC, deployment config, CI/CD, environments, and observability. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: steering-pragmatic
plugins.description: Opinionated pragmatic working style: prioritize accuracy, calibration, and decision usefulness over agreeableness. Analytical and direct by default; distinguish facts from assumptions; avoid hype and sycophancy. Includes code economy defaults (prefer deletion, stdlib, and minimal solutions over new abstractions) and comment discipline. Always-on steering as main-session instructions, plus a SubagentStart hook that injects the same discipline into every subagent in MUST register. Opt-in.

plugins.name: steering-project-structure
plugins.description: Opt-in steering: capability-first repository structure and ownership conventions -- repo layout, ownership boundaries, shared libraries, contracts, and where docs/specs/tools live.

plugins.name: steering-speckit
plugins.description: Opinionated SpecKit workflow steering: the mandatory-gated Phase 1/2/3 DAG, human-gating rules, and command reference. Opt-in -- install alongside the speckit package to adopt this specific spec-driven process.

plugins.name: steering-subagent-routing
plugins.description: Opt-in steering: model routing and verification policy for delegated subagents -- when to delegate, model/effort choice, parallel work, and who owns verification.

plugins.name: steering-toolchain-defaults
plugins.description: Opt-in steering: opinionated default stack choices for frontend, infrastructure, and quality/observability. Install to adopt these defaults when setting up or standardizing a project.

plugins.name: steering-tools-scripts
plugins.description: Opinionated conventions for repo tooling and automation: where scripts, generators, maintained CLIs, and task runners live and how they are structured. Opt-in steering.

plugins.name: typescript-quality
plugins.description: Run TypeScript or JavaScript format, lint, type-check, and test commands with the project toolchain.

plugins.name: user-journeys
plugins.description: Service-agnostic user-journey lifecycle: author end-to-end journeys as living documents (current-truth body plus a windowed delta log), validate them against the running product through whatever interface it exposes (web, desktop via MCP, CLI, TUI, API), triage mismatches with intent-gated amendment authority, report findings through a pluggable reporter (GitHub issues or a local tracker), and run multi-journey campaigns with a bounded dispatch-coder fix loop. Ships six skills (init, write, verify, verify-changed, consolidate, campaign), two agents (journey-scribe, journey-validator), the journey format spec and templates, and a deterministic index/lint script.

plugins.name: verify
plugins.description: Run and report a final local verification pass (tests, types, build, lint) before handoff, commit, push, merge, or PR.

plugins.name: web-fetch
plugins.description: Retrieve current or URL-specific information from the web with source-aware tool routing for fetching, browsing, citing, and verifying online.

plugins.name: whats-new
plugins.description: Research what changed in a tool, CLI, library, framework, package, or dependency — or a technology, cloud service, hosted API, platform, or model family (AWS Bedrock, Anthropic/Claude, OpenAI, GCP, Azure, …) — between what is in use and the latest: breaking changes, deprecations, new features, and fixes. Resolves versions, repos, changelogs, release notes, commit logs, and service announcement feeds/APIs via machine endpoints instead of reading rendered pages, then summarizes into a fixed template.

plugins.name: write-agentic
plugins.description: Author or update skills, steering, or agent definitions using standard machine-language templates and a lint script that validates them.

plugins.name: write-docs
plugins.description: Author and review READMEs, consumer docs, PR descriptions, and internal docs: objective, example-backed, written for the released artifact, and slop-free. Ships a deterministic slop/status-language linter, plus a SubagentStart hook that injects the same documentation discipline into every subagent.
